subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Critical Period
description: A quick, practical guide to The Critical Period.

hook.text: Genie was found at age 13, locked away since birth. She never fully learned grammar despite years of therapy.

buildup.text: Lenneberg proposed a critical period for language: a window that closes around puberty.

discovery.text: Children who learn a second language before age 7 typically achieve native-level grammar. After 15, almost none do.

twist.text: Vocabulary keeps growing throughout life. But the grammar circuit has a biological clock.

climax.text: A study of 670,000 English learners confirmed the critical period ends sharply at 17.4 years.

punchline.text: Grammar has a deadline. Vocabulary doesn't.

quiz.question: When does the critical period for language grammar close?

details.summary: There is a critical period for language acquisition, roughly before puberty, after which acquiring native-level fluency becomes extremely difficult. Evidence comes from tragic cases of isolated children and from studies showing that later age of exposure consistently predicts lower ultimate fluency.
details.whyItMatters: The critical period has practical implications for when to introduce second languages and for understanding why adult language learning is harder.
takeaways: Language acquisition is easiest before puberty
Later exposure predicts lower ultimate proficiency
Brain plasticity for language narrows with age

faq.question: What happens if a child misses the critical period?
faq.answer: Cases like Genie, who was isolated until age 13, show that first language acquisition after the critical period results in severely impaired grammar despite extensive training.

faq.question: Can adults still learn a second language well?
faq.answer: Adults can become highly proficient and functional in a second language, but reaching native-like pronunciation and implicit grammar mastery is rare after puberty. Adults compensate with explicit learning strategies, broader world knowledge, and motivation.
